I'm not clear the purpose of this @IanMayo ?

Sure - happy to explain :-)

This is the idea..  We have 4 types of channel,  one is mapping.  If we make changes to the mapping channel configs, I hope that only `mapping` specific files would get edited.   Then we _know_ that we can't accidentally break another type of channel. Currently, the `mapping` props are in the same file as the other channel types.  So, adding a new mapping prop, and "tidying up the file" could mean that we accidentally change the props for another channel type.

ah I see what you mean. Yep, the mapping type is in the same file with other channel types but it's a separate type object, we can change it without effects to others. But we can move it into the channel file. I will update

You'll see that because I am crazy, I have tried to use generics to declare the props.  To do this I had to switch from `type` to `interfaces`.  This doesn't seem to introduce any compiler warnings, and things seem to work ok.

It would still be _neat_ to declare the types in channel-specific files, if we can.  Aah, the `props` for `CustomChannelProps` are only accessed from `custom.tsx` - so I guess we could just declare it in `custom.tsx`.

issues.title: Refactor Channels Admin page (modularize)
issues.body:
The Channels Admin Page code is quite complex, since it contains custom editors for different types of channel.

We should _modularise_ it - by pulling custom implementations into their own file.

The benefit of this, is that only files with code for the particular channel type would be edited in one PR, and it makes the file(s) easier to understand.

_Ideally_ we would define an interface that channel-type editors have to implement, then let the channel editors provide suitable instances.

I _guess_ the interface would include:
* custom config panels
* convert data to row
* convert row to data
* row headings
